$comment: Servicios links a service to its charge by NAME: an expense in the
Servicios category whose note folds to the same key as a service's name
IS that month's charge. A recurring rule can therefore close a service's
month by filing under its name — which is why the rule editor offers the
list rather than a text box.
apps/ios/Gastos/Core/ServiceLogic.swift nameKey) and the two are not the
same code: one strips combining marks after NFD, the other asks Foundation
for a diacritic- and case-insensitive folding. They agree on everything
They do NOT agree on one thing, deliberately left alone:
ss-folding is a German convention that Foundation applies and NFD cannot,
since ß carries no combining mark. Making them agree would mean editing a
fold that existing service names already run through, to serve a character
that cannot appear in this household's bills. Recorded here so the next
person finds the answer instead of the surprise.

differentKey.why: a longer name is a different service
punctuation is part of the name
a typo does not link, which is the point of the picker
an empty note links to nothing
